newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK said to consult public on telecom market.
newsitem.headline: HK said to consult public on telecom market.

text.p: The Hong Kong government has begun public consultations on the future of the territory's telecommunications industry as it prepares to open to foreign operators next year, Hong Kong newspapers said on Sunday.
The consultation period, aimed at gathering the public's views on the matter, will last to April 11, the reports said.
The government plans to open the telecommunications market early next year, when a World Trade Organisation agreement to liberalise global telecommunications markets comes into effect.
Sixty-nine countries including Hong Kong agreed to the accord, which was reached on February 15 and goes into effect next January.

The newspapers quoted Alex Arena, director of the territory's Telecommunications Authority, as saying the government was to hold talks with Hongkong Telecommunications Ltd on an early end to its monopoly on international calls.

Although Hongkong Telecom now has local competitors in the overseas-call market, it still has a theoretical monopoly on cross-border calls from the territory until 2006 as competitors have to route their international traffic through Hongkong Telecom lines.
Arena also said that when the WTO agreement comes into effect, rates for international calls from Hong Kong could be slashed by up to 90 percent from current rates.
That could result in a hike in the cost of local calls as income from international calls subsidises local rates, the papers said. Hong Kong Telecom is the sole provider of local service.
